title: How to Find Your IMEI Number and Block a Stolen Phone via CEIR Portal
metaTitle: Find IMEI & Block Stolen Phone via CEIR Portal (Step-by-Step 2026)
metaDescription: Lost or had your phone stolen? Learn how to retrieve your 15-digit IMEI number without the physical phone and block the handset nationwide via the CEIR portal.
metaKeywords: block stolen phone ceir, find imei number lost phone, ceir portal tracking stolen phone, check imei number without phone, unblock found phone ceir
excerpt: When your phone is lost or stolen, blocking the handset via India's CEIR portal turns the physical hardware into an unusable brick across all telecom networks.
description: Exhaustive guide on finding your 15-digit IMEI number without the physical handset and filing a nationwide block request via the Central Equipment Identity Register (CEIR).
altImage: Diagram demonstrating how to find an IMEI number from Google Find My Device and submit a blocking request on the CEIR portal

faq.title: Can a thief use a stolen phone if they factory reset it or change the SIM card?
faq.description: If the phone is blocked on the CEIR portal, changing the SIM card or performing a hardware factory data reset will NOT make it usable. CEIR blacklists the hardware IMEI number across all Indian cellular operators (Jio, Airtel, Vi, BSNL). Any SIM card inserted into the device will be immediately denied network registration and trigger an automatic location alert to law enforcement.

faq.title: How can I find my phone's IMEI number if I threw away the original retail packaging box?
faq.description: You can find your IMEI online in seconds: log into Google Find My Device (google.com/android/find) using the Google Account linked to the phone, click the Gear (Info) icon next to your device name, and Google will display your IMEI number, model name, and date of first registration.

faq.title: Can I unblock my phone if police recover it or if I find it later?
faq.description: Yes! CEIR provides an 'Unblock Found Mobile' facility. You simply submit your original Request ID, your registered mobile number, and the reason for unblocking. The device's IMEI is removed from the national blacklist within 24 hours, restoring full cellular functionality.

html:
The Immediate Crisis of a Stolen Smartphone

Having your smartphone snatched by a pickpocket or misplacing it in an auto-rickshaw or metro station is an excruciating experience. Beyond the financial loss of a modern device, the handset contains your personal identity: active UPI banking applications, private photo albums, WhatsApp communication histories, and authenticated email accounts. In previous years, thieves simply discarded the victim's SIM card, executed a hardware recovery factory reset, and resold the handset in gray markets within hours.

Today, the regulatory and technological landscape in India has fundamentally shifted. Through the Department of Telecommunications' (DoT) Central Equipment Identity Register (CEIR) integrated into the Sanchar Saathi initiative, citizens possess the power to blacklist their stolen device nationwide. Once blacklisted, the smartphone's hardware IMEI is banned across every cellular tower in India. Even if the thief changes the SIM card or flashes customized firmware, the phone cannot connect to any network and alerts police the second a new SIM is inserted. This exhaustive tutorial explains how to locate your 15-digit IMEI without the original phone and submit a binding CEIR block request.

What Is an IMEI and How Does Network Blacklisting Function?

The International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) is a globally unique 15-digit decimal code allocated by the GSMA to identify individual mobile hardware stations. Dual-SIM smartphones possess two distinct IMEI numbers (IMEI 1 and IMEI 2), one for each physical or virtual radio modem transceiver.

When a smartphone connects to a cellular tower (eNodeB or gNodeB), the network requests the device's IMEI alongside the SIM card's International Mobile Subscriber Identity (IMSI) during the initial radio resource control (RRC) handshake. CEIR connects the databases of all Indian telecom service providers (Jio, Airtel, Vodafone Idea, and BSNL) into three synchronized lists:

  • White List: All verified, legally imported and manufactured handsets permitted to access Indian telecommunications networks.
  • Grey List: Devices under observation for non-conformance or administrative verification.
  • Black List: Handsets reported lost, stolen, or cloned. When a device on the Black List attempts to connect to any tower in India, network access is instantly rejected, and the tower captures the IMSI of the inserted SIM card and transmits the geographical cell ID coordinates directly to the assigned state police cyber cell.

How to Find Your IMEI Number Without the Physical Phone

Most victims do not memorize their 15-digit IMEI numbers, and the original cardboard packaging box is often lost or discarded. Fortunately, you can retrieve your IMEI through three verified remote channels:

Method A: Via Google Find My Device (The Fastest 30-Second Method)

  1. Open any web browser on a computer or secondary phone and navigate to: https://www.google.com/android/find.
  2. Sign in with the exact Google Account that was active on the lost smartphone.
  3. In the left sidebar, select the lost smartphone from your registered device list.
  4. Look next to the device name at the top left and click the small circular Information (i) / Gear icon.
  5. A pop-up modal will immediately appear displaying:
    • IMEI Number: Your primary 15-digit hardware IMEI.
    • First Registered Date: The exact date the device was first linked to Google servers.
    • Last Seen Timestamp: The exact date and time the phone last communicated with Google location services.
  6. Copy and write down this 15-digit number immediately.

Method B: Via Your E-Commerce Purchase Invoice (Amazon, Flipkart, Retail Stores)

Under Indian consumer protection regulations, all registered electronic retailers are legally required to print the device's primary IMEI number directly on the tax invoice:

  • Open your Amazon or Flipkart app on a friend's phone or computer.
  • Go to Your Orders > locate the smartphone purchase > tap Download Invoice.
  • Examine the product description line. You will observe: 'Model: Galaxy S24 Ultra, IMEI: 35894120XXXXXXXX'.
  • If purchased from an offline retail store (Croma, Reliance Digital, Vijay Sales), check the physical or digital GST bill sent to your registered email or WhatsApp.

Method C: Dialing the Universal USSD Code (For Future Preparedness)

If you currently possess a working phone, take 5 seconds right now to dial: *#06# on your phone dialer. Your device will display a barcode card containing IMEI 1, IMEI 2, and the hardware serial number. Take a screenshot and email it to yourself.

Step-by-Step: Submitting the CEIR Blocking Request

Before accessing the CEIR portal, ensure you have the three mandatory prerequisites:

  1. Digital Police Lost Report (LDR) or e-FIR: You do NOT need to visit a physical police station. Almost every state police department in India (Delhi Police, Maharashtra Police, UP Police, Karnataka Police, etc.) operates a mobile app or web portal where you can file an Online Lost Article Report in 3 minutes and download a PDF receipt containing a valid LDR/FIR number.
  2. Duplicate SIM Card: Visit your nearest Jio, Airtel, or Vi store with your Aadhaar card and obtain a replacement SIM for the mobile number that was inside the stolen phone. You need this because CEIR sends a verification OTP to the registered owner's phone number during submission.
  3. Digital Copy of Purchase Bill or Police Report PDF.

Navigating the CEIR Portal

  1. Visit the official Government of India portal: https://www.ceir.gov.in (or access via sanchar-saathi.gov.in).
  2. Click on the prominent red button labeled: 'Block Stolen/Lost Mobile'.
  3. Fill Device Information:
    • Enter Mobile Number 1 (the SIM number in Slot 1).
    • Enter Mobile Number 2 (if dual-SIM).
    • Input IMEI 1 (15 digits) and IMEI 2 (if known).
    • Select Device Brand (e.g., Samsung, Apple, Vivo) and Device Model.
    • Upload the scanned copy of the purchase invoice (optional but accelerates processing).
  4. Fill Lost Information:
    • Specify the Lost Place (street/city/landmark) and State/District.
    • Select the exact Date and Time the incident occurred.
    • Select the Police Station jurisdiction and enter the Police Complaint Number (LDR/FIR).
    • Upload the PDF copy of your Police Lost Report.
  5. Fill Mobile Owner Personal Information:
    • Owner Name, Physical Address, and Upload an Identity Proof (Aadhaar, Voter ID, PAN, or Driving License).
    • Enter an active mobile number to receive the submission OTP. Enter the OTP and tick the declaration checkbox.
  6. Click Submit. The portal will generate a unique Request ID (e.g., REQ-2026-984215). Save this Request ID securely.

What Happens Next? The Enforcement Pipeline

Once submitted, the CEIR backend executes the following automated actions within 24 hours:

  1. The IMEI is added to the National Central Blacklist across all telecom operators.
  2. If the phone is currently turned on, cellular towers terminate the active data and voice session. The status bar displays 'Emergency Calls Only' or 'No Service'.
  3. When a thief or secondary buyer inserts a new SIM card, the carrier tower intercepts the pairing, denies network registration, logs the new subscriber's IMSI, and automatically flags the location in the respective State Police Cyber Cell dashboard for physical recovery.

Method D: Finding IMEI for Apple iPhone & iPad (For Mixed Households)

If you or a family member had an iPhone stolen, Apple provides a centralized web interface to retrieve the IMEI without the device:

  1. Navigate to https://appleid.apple.com on any browser.
  2. Sign in with your Apple ID and master password.
  3. Under the Devices section, locate the stolen iPhone and click on its name.
  4. A detailed modal will open displaying the device model, serial number, and both IMEI 1 and IMEI 2 (eSIM) numbers.
  5. Record both numbers immediately for the CEIR submission form.

What Happens Across State Lines? Nationwide Inter-Carrier Coordination

In the past, smartphone theft syndicates relied on cross-state logistics: a device stolen in New Delhi or Mumbai was quickly transported by train or courier to West Bengal, Bihar, or Rajasthan to be resold on local used-market platforms. Thieves operated under the assumption that local state police forces would not coordinate cross-border IMEI tracking.

The CEIR portal neutralizes this criminal strategy completely. Because CEIR operates at the federal Department of Telecommunications (DoT) level, the national blacklist is replicated synchronously across all 22 telecom circles in India (including Metro circles and state-level circles). The moment a buyer or thief in Guwahati, Jaipur, or Kochi inserts a local SIM card into a handset stolen in Bengaluru, the target tower notifies the centralized DoT server. The server automatically routes an automated telecommunication trace alert containing the cell tower sector ID and the new subscriber's Aadhaar-verified mobile number to the investigating police officer who issued the original FIR or Lost Report.

How to Unblock the Phone When Recovered

If local police recover your smartphone or you locate it in lost-and-found, restoring it is straightforward:

  1. Go back to https://www.ceir.gov.in.
  2. Click on the green button: 'Un-Block Found Mobile'.
  3. Enter your original Request ID, the phone number you used for OTP during blocking, and select the reason for unblocking (e.g., 'Recovered by Police' or 'Found by Self').
  4. Submit the OTP. Within 24 hours, the national blacklist is updated, and your handset regains full 4G/5G cellular voice and data capabilities.

Comprehensive Anti-Theft Strategy

A smartphone theft defense plan requires layered security. In conjunction with CEIR blocking, ensure you follow our companion tutorials on enabling Android Anti-Theft Protection and Remote Lock, learn how to lock your Aadhaar biometrics to prevent fraudulent SIM re-issuance, and audit your linked banking sessions with our guide on canceling active UPI mandates across payment apps.
